summary: Implement manifest-bound per-account connector capability settings with default deny, immutable tenant-scoped revisions, explicit read/write risk metadata, audit evidence and sync execution guards within the frozen Connector SDK and approval architecture.

impacts.evidence: Capability revisions carry organization and workspace identity, use authenticated scope only and are protected by forced PostgreSQL RLS.
Capability snapshots contain operation identifiers and policy metadata only; no credentials, remote payloads or personal data are persisted.
OpenAPI 0.9.0 adds one additive replacement operation and capability metadata to connector account responses; generated SDKs are regenerated.
No event type or canonical envelope changes; immutable application audit records carry the change evidence.
Frozen Connector and Runtime roots are unchanged; additive host-owned capability direction and risk metadata extends the existing registry.
Expand migration 000060 adds append-only complete capability snapshots and leaves existing accounts default-denied without destructive backfill.
Only manifest-declared capabilities can be enabled, absent state denies, and activation and sync execution fail closed on missing grants.
All remote writes are classified write_sensitive with approval_required=true by host metadata that clients and manifests cannot downgrade.
Every replacement advances the account version and appends bounded audit evidence with enabled and write counts; snapshots remain immutable.
Sync policy creation, re-enabling and manual execution authorize the current account snapshot before creating a durable run.
No new destination or egress path is introduced; webhook receive capabilities remain read-classified account grants.
Denied capability operations return explicit 422 responses and successful configuration changes carry immutable audit counts.
Operators can replace the selection with an empty set for immediate default deny; prior revisions are retained rather than rolled back destructively.
Unit, migration, OpenAPI parity, generated SDK and frontend build checks cover manifest rejection, default deny, risk classification and routing.
